news.title: New major risk - Shareholder dilution
news.body: The company's shareholders have been substantially diluted in the past year. Increase in shares outstanding: 58% This is considered a major risk. Shareholder dilution occurs when there is an increase in the number of shares on issue that is not proportionally distributed between all shareholders. Often due to the company raising equity capital or some options being converted into stock. All else being equal, if there are more shares outstanding then each existing share will be entitled to a lower proportion of the company's total earnings, thus reducing earnings per share (EPS). While dilution might not always result in lower EPS (like if the company is using the capital to fund an EPS accretive acquisition) in a lot cases it does, along with lower dividends per share and less voting power

news.title: Gayatri Projects Limited announced that it has received INR 1.09 billion in funding from Vishwa Infrastructures and Services Pvt Ltd., Antara Asset Management Co Ltd, Zeal Global Opportunities Fund, GKC Projects Pvt Ltd. and other investors.
news.body: On April 20, 2626, Gayatri Projects Limited has closed and issued 109,000,000 equity shares at the price of INR 10 including premium of INR 8 for the gross proceeds of INR 1,090,000,000. The transaction involves the new investor participation of Vishwa Infrastructures and Services Pvt Ltd for 15,000,000 shares, GKC Projects Ltd for 15,000,000 shares, Antara India Evergreen Fund for 35,000,000 shares, M7 Global Fund PCC - Aerion for 5,000,000 shares, Zeal Global Opportunities Fund for 15,000,000 shares, Vivek Mundra for 14,000,000 shares, and Aniruddh Mundra for 10,000,000 shares. The transaction has been approved by board of directors, Stock exchange and Regulatory.

news.title: New major risk - Negative shareholders equity
news.body: The company has negative equity. Total equity: -₹14b This is considered a major risk. Being in negative equity means that the company's liabilities exceed its assets, meaning it owes more to creditors than it has in owned assets. While this doesn't mean the company is about to collapse, in the long-term, this is unsustainable. The company may have issues meeting financial obligations, is at risk of becoming insolvent and may have difficulty raising capital, especially more debt, if needed. Currently, the following risks have been identified for the company: Major Risks Debt is not well covered by operating cash flow (0.9% operating cash flow to total debt). Shares are highly illiquid. Negative equity (-₹14b). Minor Risk Market cap is less than US$100m (₹2.41b market cap, or US$26.6m).
